_comment: Validation gates for the PostGIS cost model, fixed BEFORE the held-out corpus (seed 20261107) was run. They are not tuned after looking at held-out results; any later change must be a new commit that says why.

definitions.regret: selected_actual_ms / best_actual_ms over the engines that produced a correct result for the case
definitions.prediction_ratio: max(pred/actual, actual/pred) with both floored at prediction_ratio_floor_ms (10 ms since the 2026-10-26 amendment; 1 ms before)
definitions.actual_ms: median of the warm repetitions when there are any, else the first run (cases above 30 s are run once); engine `execute` wall time, planning excluded
unsafe_selection: the selected engine failed (timeout, cancel, error) on a case the other engine completed
PostGIS selected although the semi-join risk policy blocks the shape
PostGIS selected on a source/index state that is not `available`
a plan the selected engine cannot reach (residency / unsupported operation)
definitions.merely_slower: NOT unsafe: it is regret and absolute penalty

amendments.made_after_seeing: fresh set seed 20261115 (indexed_bbox and aggregate had P90 regret 1.00 but P90 prediction ratio 3.29 / 3.12 against the 3.0 gate)
amendments.change: prediction ratio is computed with BOTH predicted and actual time floored at prediction_ratio_floor_ms = 10 (was 1 ms). All other gates unchanged.
amendments.why: after the PostGIS connector latency fix the indexed classes run in 1-3 ms (77 % of indexed_bbox times are < 10 ms); in calibration + A + B DuckDB was never faster than 64 ms in these classes, so a prediction error below 10 ms cannot change which engine is chosen. A ratio on 1-3 ms values measures timer-scale noise, not planning quality.
amendments.validation_of_the_amendment: the amended gate is NOT satisfied by the fresh set's own results; classes are promoted only by an independent confirmation set (seed 20261119) generated and committed after this amendment.
amendments.also_reported: the 1 ms-floor ratios are printed next to the amended ones in every evaluation
